newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark sees 20 pct interconnect cuts.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark sees 20 pct interconnect cuts.

text.p: Danish telecoms group Tele Danmark said on Tuesday that modernisation could allow cuts of up to 20 percent in its network access rates for competitors within three years but it ruled out immediate cuts.
"I can readily envisage interconnect access rate cuts of the order of 10 to 20 percent in the next two or three years," Tele Danmark executive Tom Togsverd told Reuters.
"We are constantly trying to modernise our network and the improvements we achieve will obviously also be of benefit to our interconnect clients," he said.
But he said the present system left no margin for cuts.
"Every penny reflects network costs, If you subtract outgoings you are left with three percent profit, so we would lose money if we cut prices now," he said.
On Monday, one of Tele Danmark's main competitors, Sweden's Telia, predicted that interconnect tariffs would soon fall to a third of Tele Danmark's current rate of 0.18 crowns per minute.
The Danish government is preparing a bill on interconnection as part of deregulation of the country's telecoms industry and the legislation is expected to be in place by the end of March.
Tele Danmark protested last month gainst the draft bill.
The 52 percent state-owned former monopoly said the new law would usher in far lower rates for competitor access to its network than EU rules demanded and could hit profits hard.
Denmark's telecommunications union said last week that the legislation in its present form could mean a direct drop in profits for Tele Danmark of around one billion crowns annually.
The Danish telecommunications sector was deregulated on July 1, 1996 but a final phase of enabling legislation is still pending.
